context.name: Context
context.audience: Anyone new to UDP, including non-engineers
context.blurb: UDP among the systems that call it. Every caller is a GOV.UK Once system in its own AWS account; the person never reaches UDP directly, and nothing outside the programme does either. C4 level 1 — runtime only.
context.note: The consumers a deployment admits are an SSM parameter, not code. The two named here are the ones the committed development context lists.

request.name: Request path
request.audience: On-call, and anyone tracing a consumer call
request.blurb: Every hop a consumer call takes, numbered in reading order, with the identity exchange as the worked example: it is the call FLEX makes to turn its own user id into another service's, and it meets every gate on the way in.
request.note: Three gates before a function runs — the VPC endpoint the call came through, the SigV4 signature, and the WAF — and one thing that looks like a gate and is not: the API key.
request.dashMeans: a header the gateway reads but never checks

containers.name: Containers
containers.audience: UDP engineers, and anyone reviewing a change to a stack
containers.blurb: Every separately deployable part the CDK app creates per environment, grouped by the stack that owns it, and the traffic between them. C4 level 2.
containers.note: The VPC stack is on Network; the monitoring, backup, Macie and test stacks are on Security and Delivery. Counts on the boxes are of functions as deployed; the Resources tab binds them to the synthesised templates.

components.name: Components
components.audience: Engineers changing a handler — this is the code, not the infrastructure
components.blurb: Inside one route Lambda: the middleware every request runs through, in the order it runs, and the data-access layer beneath the handler. All thirteen route functions are wired the same way. C4 level 3.
components.note: Read the chain top to bottom for a request coming in, and bottom to top for the response going out: the serialiser and sanitiser are after middleware, so they run on the way back.
components.dashMeans: a hand-off inside the library, not a call the handler makes

rights.name: Rights requests
rights.audience: Anyone answering a subject access or deletion request, and anyone reviewing how they are met
rights.blurb: The two asynchronous flows side by side, numbered in reading order: an export that ends in a seven-day download link, and a deletion that ends with the person's links gone. Both answer 202 at the API and do the work off a queue.
rights.note: Neither flow tells the consumer when it is done. An export is polled for; a deletion has no status route at all.
rights.dashMeans: where a failure goes — and nothing in the repository reads either dead-letter queue

network.name: Network
network.audience: Anyone changing a subnet, an endpoint or a security group
network.blurb: The one VPC per environment, its three subnet tiers, and the endpoints that are the only way out of the isolated tier. Every Lambda sits in the isolated tier; everything it reaches is an endpoint beside it.
network.note: The private API is not in the VPC. It is a regional service that accepts calls only through the execute-api endpoints its resource policy lists — the consumers' own, and this VPC's, which the test builds use. The test builds also reach CodeBuild and ECR through the interface endpoints; that edge is a fact on their box.

security.name: Security
security.audience: Security review, on-call, and anyone answering an audit question
security.blurb: The controls that bound every box on the other tabs, in five columns: who may call, what is encrypted and with which key, what watches, what wakes someone, and what can be restored.
security.note: The alarms are all against the same NFR constants the performance tests use: p95 under 200 ms at the API, 150 ms in a function, errors under 0.1%.

delivery.name: Delivery
delivery.audience: Anyone shipping a change, and on-call
delivery.blurb: Three zones: what a pull request gets, what a merge to main ships and where it stops, and the test infrastructure in the account that both use. Every step is a GitHub Actions job or a CodeBuild project; read each zone top to bottom.
delivery.note: The path from a merge to production is one workflow with no manual step in it. Whether a GitHub environment holds a required reviewer is configured outside the repository and is not shown here.
delivery.dashMeans: a step that starts something and does not wait for it, or a trigger rather than a dependency

resources.name: Resources
resources.audience: Cost, audit and incident scoping — the detail behind every badge
resources.blurb: Every AWS resource the CDK app declares, counted per environment from the CloudFormation it synthesises.
resources.note: Counts follow the stage selector. The synth runs without AWS credentials, so every SSM lookup resolves to its default: the consumer config is empty and only the built-in test consumer is counted. A real deployment adds a role, a secret, a usage plan and an API key per consumer, and one KMS key for the secrets. Nothing in the VPC is counted twice for a pull-request deployment: the VPC stack is shared per environment.
